COUNT-ASYMMETRIC, 59 vs 58, and the cause is nameable from the aligned view: the offsets are already shifted by 4 at +0xa8, so the extra instruction is an fmr inside the expanded helper - a value-returning helper gives the guarded value its own parameter web, so the d<=0 fall-through path needs a copy that retail does not have. That is positive evidence that retail's source updates `d` IN PLACE inside the guard, which is what the tree already does; the inline-helper reconstruction of this kernel is refuted for this function. (2) SEED STORAGE CLASS: `register f32 best_dist = 100000.0f;` -> `register f32 best_dist = lbl_803468B0;`, using the `extern f32 lbl_803468B0;` ALREADY DECLARED at line 224 of this very TU and already used at line 751, and matching the sibling idiom `f32 best_dist = lbl_803468B0;` that game/enemy/enemy.c carries at four nearest-search loops. 40 words, and the aligned view over 0x10:0x34 is register-for-register identical to HEAD - but the +0x14 relocation moved from the anonymous @1058 to retail's own @lbl_803468B0, a strict relocation-identity gain at zero register cost. NOT KEPT, see `residual`. (3) ALL FOUR CONSTANTS AS RETAIL POOL EXTERNS: seed as above, `if (d > 0.0f)` -> `if (d > lbl_80346820)`, and `0.5`/`3.0` -> `lbl_80346830`/`lbl_803468B8` at all four refinement sites, with `extern f64 lbl_803468B8;` added before the function. 40 words at 58/58, ALL FOUR relocations now naming the target's own pool objects - and the FPR assignment MOVED: HEAD's descending group {acc f6, d f5, guard f4, half f3, three f2} became {acc f6, half f5, three f4, d f3, guard f2}. attributes.residual: The rule stays. THE MECHANISM, restated more sharply than v1: our assignment is retail's with the accumulator INSERTED at the top of the descending group. Retail: f6=d, f5=guard(0.0f), f4=half(0.5), f3=three(3.0), f0=best_dist, scratch f1,f2,f7,f8. Ours: f6=best_dist, f5=d, f4=guard, f3=half, f2=three, scratch f0,f1,f7,f8. The other four webs keep retail's exact relative order; the whole 40-word gap is that one insertion, and it is not a pressure effect - both streams use f0-f8 and leave f9-f13 free. WHY THE SEED-ONLY FORM WAS NOT KEPT even though it is a strict relocation-identity gain at zero register cost: `defake_gate.py check game/game/gamemain` exits 1 on it with a DIRECTION-UNKNOWN verdict, because removing one anonymous pool entry renumbers @1059-@1061 to @1058-@1060 and the gate cannot resolve an @NN name; its own text confirms the one row that matters ('our new symbol MATCHES it' for lbl_803468B0) and reports the other three as neither-old-nor-new-matching, i.e. unchanged in correctness. The gain is real but score-invisible, it costs a TU-wide anonymous-pool renumber, and it is one line - so it is banked here for a de-fakematch lane that owns gamemain to take deliberately, rather than pushed past a red gate for zero score. The exact edit is in `probed_form` (2).

hypothesis.cheapest_refuting_observation: Count the volatile FPRs each stream leaves UNUSED. If the target is at the ceiling, the insertion reading is wrong and this is a pressure problem with a different cure. Measured 2026-09-03 over the whole aligned view: both streams use exactly f0-f8 of the fourteen volatile FPRs, leaving f9-f13 free in BOTH - so there is no pressure anywhere in this function and the difference is purely allocation ORDER, which is what makes the insertion reading the right one and also what makes a pressure-raising cure pointless here.
hypothesis.screened_against_target: yes - the nine-versus-nine FPR count, the two f0 writes in the target, the accumulator seed at +0x14, the three constant registers at +0x20/+0x28/+0x2c and the accumulator update at +0xcc were read from the aligned raw view against the retail bytes over the whole 58-instruction body, in HEAD and in each of the three probes.
hypothesis.statement: v1 framed this as 'which register carries the loop-carried minimum'. The sharper framing, read off the aligned view this run, is that our assignment is retail's assignment with ONE web INSERTED: retail assigns the descending group f6..f3 as {d, guard, half, three} and puts the accumulator in f0, while we assign f6..f2 as {accumulator, d, guard, half, three} - the same relative order for the other four, with the accumulator pushed in at the top and everything else shifted down one. So the question is not which register the accumulator gets but why it JOINS the group at all, and the untried axis is INTERFERENCE: give the accumulator a live range that conflicts with the group's members (for instance by reading `best_dist` inside the guarded rsqrt block, or by making the loop body's last statement depend on it) so it cannot be coloured alongside them. A second untried axis, cheap and independent: the pre-loop block currently materialises the seed BEFORE `cmpwi`/`mtctr`; a form that sinks the seed load after the loop-count setup would test whether the group is formed in emission order.
